content.comment_body: I have a program that was supplied by an external party who is no longer available. There are eight [product_name] controllers managing door access with magnetic locks. Each door unit needs to communicate its status (open/closed) to the other seven devices, and also read their respective statuses. From my understanding, each controller supports up to eight network connections, but I may be misapplying the logic in network mode. When I link an output from one controller to an input on another, the input activates and an IP address is assigned. After establishing eight such connections, the system prevents adding any further network links. Any suggestions would be appreciated.
Your PDF document isn't helpful. Please show your actual network project instead. Upload it as a ZIP archive.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is operating a distributed door access setup using eight [product_name] controllers and is encountering a limitation in the number of allowed network connections per device. This restriction is affecting both system scalability and the capacity to share status information among all devices. There is uncertainty regarding the proper way to set up the networking logic, and the user shows some frustration upon reaching the device connection limit.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to interconnect all eight [product_name] controllers so that each device can both send and receive status updates from the others, without running into networking configuration constraints.
